./.title: Strata for FM-1
./.body:
Strata for FM-1
Strata turns the M-VAVE FM-1 into a complete pocket instrument: a deep wavetable synth, an 8-track looper
and a drum machine.


Synth: two wavetable oscillators on 54 tables, sub, noise, a filter, envelopes, drawable LFOs, eight voices.
Effects: a chain of up to eight from thirteen types.
Playing: scales, chords on every key, strum, an arpeggiator with sixteen steps, macros, tap tempo.
Looper: synth, MIDI and drum tracks, clips in eight scenes, overdubs, recorded knob moves, four projects.
Drums: seven drum models, 64 presets, six kits, a step grid, Euclidean fills, a sidechain duck.

This book

Guide: get started and see every feature on one page.
Cheat sheet: every button and knob.
Manual: each feature in depth, starting with The panel.

Install
Open the site's Install page in Chrome or Edge on a computer, with the FM-1 on a USB data cable.
Steps and recovery: Installing and recovery.

Back up first. Strata keeps its presets, projects and drum library in the flash area where Felucca keeps its
projects and samples. Saving anything in Strata can overwrite them, and going back to Felucca or the official
firmware does not restore them. A full flash backup is the only way back to exactly what you had
(how). Strata never writes the boot area, calibration, Bluetooth pairing or the
unit's keys.

Disclaimer
Strata is independent, unofficial firmware, not affiliated with or endorsed by M-VAVE or the FM-1's owners, nor by
Felucca's author or Hügelton Instruments.
It is provided as is, without any warranty (GPL-3.0, sections 15 and 16). Installing firmware other than the
official one can leave the FM-1 unusable until it is recovered; you install it at your own risk. Strata is a
pre-release. Strata was created entirely with Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic.
Strata is a modified version of Felucca, Copyright (C) 2026 Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments,
licensed GPL-3.0-only like it. The screen uses Space Mono (SIL OFL 1.1). Source, notices and licences are on the site.

guide/guide.html.title: Guide
guide/guide.html.body:
Guide
Strata turns the FM-1 into a wavetable synth, an 8-track looper and a drum machine. This page gets you playing and
shows every feature at a glance; each card links to its chapter of the Manual. Every button is on the
cheat sheet.
Quick start


Install. Open the site's Install page in Chrome or Edge, make a backup, then press Find the FM-1 and
Write Strata (how).
Play. Switch the FM-1 on. HOME shows the sound. Play the keys; OCT− and OCT+ change the
octave, and MASTER sets the level.
Pick a sound. Turn PRESETS to choose a preset from the list, then press SAVE twice to load it.
Change it. Press EDIT. Turn SELECT to choose a module (OSC A, OSC B, SUB, NOISE, FILTER, MATRIX),
ALGORITHM to choose a page, and KNOB 1 to 4 to set the values. Hold EDIT and press OCT+ to
switch the module shown on.
Save it. Press SAVE. In the window, SAVE AS NEW is chosen for a sound you haven't saved before
(OCT− and OCT+ move the choice). Press SAVE to confirm, then SAVE again
to keep the suggested name.

Hold HOME on any screen to see what every control does there. SAVE + OCT− undoes your
last change.

manual/panel.html.title: The panel
manual/panel.html.body:
The panel
How Strata uses the FM-1's controls and screen, and the rules every menu follows. The
cheat sheet lists every button in one table.
The controls



Control
What it does




Keys (F3 to G5)
Play the selected track. On some screens they choose, launch or type instead.


OCT− OCT+
Change the keys' octave (−3 to +3). Held with a menu button, they mean off and on.


KNOB 1–4
Set the four values on the screen, left to right.


SELECT
Go to the next or previous module of the menu (EDIT: OSC A, OSC B, SUB, NOISE, FILTER, MATRIX).


ALGORITHM
Go to the next or previous page of the module.


PRESETS
Open the presets list (on looper pages: choose the track; on a drum track: choose the drum).


MASTER
Output level.



The FM-1's keys have no velocity; they play at SCL's VELOCITY (100).
The screen


Top line: the module's name, with a filled dot when it is on. The dots at the right are the menu's modules;
SELECT moves between them.
Body: a drawing of what the module does. The circled numbers are the knobs' handles, placed on what each knob
moves. A knob's handle and value turn vermilion while it turns; the shape before the turn stays dashed behind.
Bottom row: the module's pages; the one shown is highlighted. The last page, VALUES, shows the same knobs as
large numbers, and turns them in the finest steps: use it to set an exact value.
P in a square: what PRESETS chooses on this page.
Vermilion dot after a name: the sound or kit has unsaved changes.

A module that is switched off says so on its pages ("OSC B IS OFF · EDIT + OCT+ TURNS IT ON").
Knobs

Turned slowly, a knob moves its value in fine steps; turned quickly, in large ones. SETTINGS > PANEL > ACCEL off
makes every step the same size.
Knobs with a centre (PAN, TUNE, bipolar amounts) pause at the centre for a few detents, so you can find it.

Buttons

Once: opens the menu on the page you left. Pressed inside its own menu: goes to its first page.
Twice (within 300 ms): its second job, such as EDIT twice for the wavetable list.
Held: opens its layer until you let go.
With OCT+ / OCT−: hold the button, then press OCT+ to switch on or add, OCT− to switch off
or remove.
With OCT− held 5 s: resets what the menu shows. A countdown appears after 2 s; let go of OCT− to
cancel. Sound changes can be undone afterwards with SAVE + OCT−.

Help: hold HOME to see what every control does on the current screen.
Layers
Hold a button to open its layer; let go to close it. REC's and GLO's layers can stay open: press the button with
OCT+ (GLO also: twice), and tap the button to close.

The sound
A sound is two wavetable oscillators (OSC A, OSC B), a SUB oscillator and NOISE through a FILTER. Defaults for every
parameter are in the parameter reference.
HOME

HOME shows the selected track's sound, with the bloom, a ring of dots that swirls with the sound.

KNOB 1–4 are MACRO 1–4: each moves whatever the sound assigns to it (macros).
Turn SELECT to choose the track (T1 to T8); turn PRESETS to choose a sound.
ALGORITHM shows MIX 1-4 and MIX 5-8: the eight tracks' volumes on the knobs.

How to

Switch a source or the filter on: press EDIT, turn SELECT to OSC B, SUB, NOISE or FILTER, then hold
EDIT and press OCT+. (OCT− switches it off.)

manual/modulation.html.title: Envelopes, LFOs and modulation
manual/modulation.html.body:
Envelopes, LFOs and modulation
ENV 1 shapes every note's level. ENV 2, the two LFOs, the macros and the MIDI controllers move other parameters
through the matrix: eight slots, each a source, a destination and an amount. All of it is saved with the sound.
How to
Put a modulator on a knob


Go to the page with the parameter you want to move, such as FILTER's TONE page.
Press LFO twice for an LFO, or ENV twice for an envelope or a macro. The assign window opens.
Turn KNOB 1 to choose the source and KNOB 2 to choose the parameter. Parameters marked NO can't be modulated.
Turn ALGORITHM to the second page. Turn KNOB 2 to set the AMOUNT (−100 to +100 %) and KNOB 1 to set the POLARITY.
Press any button to close it. OCT− in the window removes the source from the parameter.

Try sources quickly (the MOD layer)

Hold REC. The screen lists the page's four parameters.
Press a white key to choose a source; the screen names each key's source (F3 is ENV 1, A3 LFO 1, C4 MACRO 1).
Turn a knob to set that source's depth on its parameter. Let go of REC to finish (REC + OCT+
keeps the layer open).

Draw an LFO

Press LFO. The POINTS page shows the shape as points.
KNOB 1 chooses a point, KNOB 2 moves it in time, KNOB 3 up or down, KNOB 4 bends the line after it.
LFO + OCT+ adds a point; LFO + OCT− deletes the one chosen (up to 16
points; the end points stay). Editing a built-in shape turns it into DRAWN.

Envelopes

ENV opens ENV 1 (the amp) and ENV 2 (free to assign). Times run from 1 ms to 30 s.

Polarity. A unipolar source (0…1) pushes a parameter one way; a bipolar one (−1…+1) swings it both ways. Each

A slot onto an effect, a macro or VOLUME follows the newest note's envelopes and LFOs, since the effects are shared by
all voices. VALUES pages show the range the modulation takes each parameter to.
Macros
MACRO 1–4 are HOME's four knobs, FX held (MACROS), and MIDI CC 16–19. Each moves whatever its matrix slots
point at, and a macro can itself be modulated. INIT has MACRO 1–4 in its first four slots, waiting for a destination.

Tip: one macro, several slots: MACRO 1 onto CUTOFF, RESO and the reverb's MIX turns HOME's KNOB 1 into a single
"open it up" control.

manual/fx.html.title: Effects
manual/fx.html.body:
Effects
The effects are a chain of up to eight modules, played in order, followed by a limiter. Each type can be in the chain
twice, except DELAY and REVERB (once each). The chain is part of the sound and is saved with it.
How to

Add an effect

Press FX for the chain view.
Turn KNOB 1 (or ALGORITHM) to choose a type, and KNOB 2 (or SELECT) to choose a slot. Past the last effect the
slot is + HERE.
Hold FX and press OCT+. The effect is added below the chosen slot.

Edit it: press FX twice to open the chosen effect. ALGORITHM steps its pages, SELECT moves to the next
effect in the chain. Press FX to return to the chain.
Move it: on the chain view, turn KNOB 3. Set its mix: KNOB 4.
Remove it: on the chain view, FX + OCT−. Bypass it: on its own page,
FX + OCT− (and OCT+ to bring it back), or hold FX and press its white key
(F3 for the first effect … F4 for the eighth).
Every change can be undone with SAVE + OCT−. The top line shows how many effects are in the
chain and an estimate of their processor cost; REVERB is the costliest.

manual/looper.html.title: The looper
manual/looper.html.body:
The looper
Eight tracks (T1–T8) and eight scenes (A–H). Each track can hold one clip per scene: a loop of notes and knob moves,
1 to 16 bars long. A scene is a row of clips that play together; SONG chains scenes. Four projects keep it all.
SEQ opens three modules (SELECT): LOOP (CLIPS, MIXER, SONG), CLIP (NOTES, NOTE+, CLIP, TOOLS) and
TRACK (RECORD, CLICK). On every looper page, PRESETS chooses the track. The top line shows the track, the scene, the
bar and beat, and REC or DUB while recording.
How to

Record a loop

Press SEQ. Turn PRESETS to choose a track and KNOB 2 to choose a scene with an empty place.
Tap REC. If the transport is stopped, one bar of count-in clicks plays first; if it is running,
recording starts at the next bar.
Play. Notes are recorded as played (or quantized, see RECORD), and so are turns of any knob that can be modulated.
Tap REC again. The clip is rounded to whole bars and loops at once.

Overdub: tap REC on a clip that has notes. Each pass adds to it until you tap REC again. Hold
SEQ and press F#5 (UNDO PASS) to take the last pass back.
Keep what you just played: press REC twice. TAKE puts the notes you played on the selected track (the
last 256, within 16 bars) into a new clip in the chosen scene.
Launch: on the CLIPS page, white keys 1–8 launch this scene's clips on tracks 1–8 (press again to stop), and black
keys 1–8 launch scenes A–H. A launch waits for the next bar. PLAY stops everything; press it again to
restart the clips from the top.
Make or delete a clip: SEQ + OCT+ makes an empty 1-bar clip (keep SEQ held and turn PRESETS
to set its length). SEQ + OCT− asks DELETE?; press it again to delete.
Edit notes: SELECT to CLIP. On NOTES, KNOB 1 chooses a note and KNOB 2–4 set its PITCH, START and LENGTH.

Launch or stop each track's clip in the chosen scene

Launch scenes A–H

Mute tracks 1–8

type.

manual/drums.html.title: The drums
manual/drums.html.body:
The drums
Any looper track can be a drum track (TYPE DRUMS). All drum tracks of a project play its one kit: eight drum rows
and a silent ninth row, DUCK, that ducks the synth. The drums don't go through the effects chain.
How to
Make a drum track: press SEQ, choose the track with PRESETS, turn KNOB 1 (TYPE) to DRUMS and stop.
Play: white keys 1–8 (F3–F4) play KICK, SNARE, CLAP, HAT CL, HAT OP, CYM, WT 1, WT 2; white keys 9–16 play them
accented; F#3 is DUCK. Record with REC as on any track.
Program a beat on the grid

Press SEQ, then SELECT to CLIP. The GRID page shows the clip in sixteenth steps.
Press a black key to choose the row (1 KICK … 9 DUCK).
Press white keys to put hits in or take them out on the sixteen steps shown. KNOB 1 moves to other steps.
Press PLAY.

Hold a step's key and turn the knobs to set that hit's VELOCITY, ACCENT, CHANCE and RATCHET.
Fill a row with a rhythm (EUCLID): on CLIP, ALGORITHM to EUCLID. Turn KNOB 4 to choose the row, then KNOB 1 HITS,
KNOB 2 STEPS and KNOB 3 ROTATE. Each turn refills that row across the clip.
Load a kit: press EDIT twice on HOME or KIT, turn PRESETS, press SAVE twice. Your clips stay.
Load a drum preset into a row: press EDIT (DRUM shows the drum PRESETS chooses), then EDIT
twice. SELECT changes the category, PRESETS the preset; SAVE twice loads it. The row keeps its LEVEL and PAN.
Save: on a drum track, SAVE saves the drum (on DRUM) or the kit (elsewhere) as a sound is saved: SAVE
over your own, or SAVE AS NEW with a name. You can keep 64 drum presets and 16 kits; any project can use them.
HOME on a drum track

HOME shows the kit and its eight drums, lit as they sound. PRESETS chooses the drum EDIT opens. The knobs move the
whole kit: TUNE (±24 semitones), DECAY (50–200 % of each drum's length), TONE (±50) and
DUCK (how far the synth ducks).

manual/presets.html.title: Presets and saving
manual/presets.html.body:
Presets and saving
A preset holds the whole sound: oscillators, filter, envelopes, LFOs, matrix, effects, voice and macros, with a name
(up to 16 characters) and a category. Strata has INIT, eight starter sounds (SUPERSAW, PLUCK, PAD, FM KEYS, SYNC LEAD,
LADDER BASS, VOWEL PAD, OTT GROWL) and 64 slots for yours. Tempo, scale, chords, ARP and drums are not part of a preset.
How to

Load a preset: turn PRESETS (on any page except the looper's) to open the list, choose a preset, and press
SAVE twice. The list closes by itself after 5 seconds. If the sound has unsaved changes, the list warns
"SAVE TWICE: YOUR EDITS GO"; undo brings them back.
Save


Press SAVE. The SAVE window opens.
Choose with OCT−/OCT+: SAVE writes over your preset; SAVE AS NEW makes a new one
named as the next version ("WARM PAD" → "WARM PAD v2"); CANCEL. Starter sounds and INIT can only be saved as
new.
Press SAVE. For SAVE AS NEW, NAME IT opens: edit the name if you like and press SAVE.

The category / the slot (its own slot renames it)

Write it / leave without saving



Delete a preset: in the list, choose it and press SAVE + OCT−; press it again to confirm.
Undo and redo: SAVE + OCT− and SAVE + OCT+, through the last 8 changes
to the sound (each knob gesture, assignment, effect change, LFO point and preset load).
The browser

Press SAVE twice (with no list open). KNOB 1 chooses the category (ALL, BASS, LEAD, PAD, PLUCK, KEYS, FX,
SEQ, OTHER), KNOB 2 the preset (it loads as you turn), KNOB 3 the bank (ALL, STARTER, USER). SAVE once
renames the sound playing. Hold OCT− for 3 seconds to delete the user preset playing;
SAVE + OCT− straight after puts it back. SAVE twice or HOME leaves.
What is kept
The sound playing and the settings are kept a few seconds after you stop playing, and come back at power-on. Presets
are written when you save. HOME + OCT+ / OCT− loads the next or previous preset. MIDI
program changes can load presets (MIDI and USB).

Warning: your presets, projects and drum library live in the same flash area as Felucca's projects and samples.
Saving in Strata can overwrite them. Back up before you install (how).

Move the controller. It now sets that parameter.

removes them all. Up to 32 mappings.

Send notes to a computer: set a looper track's TYPE to MIDI (or SYNTH+MIDI) and its CHANNEL on TRACK > RECORD.
Everything that track plays, including chords and the ARP, goes out on that channel.
Follow a computer's clock: GLO, SELECT to GLOBAL, set CLOCK IN to MIDI. Start, continue and stop then run

manual/install.html.title: Installing and recovery
manual/install.html.body:
Installing and recovery
Strata installs over the FM-1's own USB-MIDI update path, from a web page, as Felucca does. The firmware running now
loads the package and starts the update loader, which writes the firmware area only and restarts into Strata. About a
minute.

Disclaimer. Strata is unofficial and comes without any warranty (GPL-3.0). Installing firmware other than the
official one can leave the FM-1 unusable until it is recovered; you install it at your own risk. Strata was created entirely with Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic.
Your data. Saving anything in Strata can overwrite Felucca's projects and samples, which share the same flash.
Going back does not bring them back. A full backup does.

Back up first
A full backup is a copy of the FM-1's whole flash (1 MiB). It's the only way back to exactly what you have now,
Felucca's projects and samples included. It's recommended, not required. It's made in the chip's backup mode, with
a backup tool on a computer.
1. Put the FM-1 in backup mode, in any of these ways:

From Strata or Felucca: hold OCT− and OCT+ for 5 seconds (a countdown shows from 2 s).
With Strata V0.87 the computer may show an unknown USB device instead; then switch the FM-1 off and on and use
one of the last two ways.
From the official firmware (V15): send the USB-MIDI message F0 22 24 35 7D F7 with any program that sends
SysEx.
The FM-1 Transporter, a Seeed XIAO RP2040 wired to the FM-1's
USB lines: at power-on, whatever the firmware does.
A Flipper Zero with flipper-fm1-recovery: at power-on,
whatever the firmware does.

In backup mode the FM-1 appears as a USB disk named WL82 UBOOT1.00. If the computer offers to format it, cancel.
Never format it.
2. Read the whole flash with a backup tool, twice, and keep it only if both copies are identical:

MvaveFM1Unbricker: fm1_unbrick.py backup (Windows or Linux),
which reads twice and compares by itself.
jl-uboot-tool: read 0 0x100000 (Windows or Linux).
The FM-1 Transporter: fm1t.py dump (macOS, Linux or Windows), through its own board.
flipper-fm1-recovery's pc_backup.py (Windows).

3. Switch the FM-1 off and on to leave backup mode. Keep the backup somewhere safe.
Install

Open the site's Install page in Chrome or Edge on a computer. It checks the package and shows its SHA-256.
Connect the FM-1 with a USB data cable straight to the computer (no hub), with its battery charged. Close every
other app that uses MIDI (DAWs, M-UPGRADE, Felucca's editor).
In Before you start, make your backup (recommended), then tick the three boxes: cable and battery, other MIDI
apps closed, the data warning understood.
In Install, press Find the FM-1 and allow MIDI with SysEx when the browser asks. The page says which
firmware it found before anything is written.
Press Write Strata. Don't unplug the FM-1 or touch its power switch until the page says Done.
When asked, switch the FM-1 off and on. The page says Done once Strata answers after the restart.

To update, do the same with the new version: your presets, projects, drum library and settings stay.
Going back

Official firmware (V15): on the Install page, under Going back, choose M-VAVE's own FM-1.fwsc (checked by
its SHA-256, never uploaded) and press Return to official V15. M-VAVE's own updater also works.
Felucca: use Felucca's installer at hugelton.github.io/Felucca; it finds
the FM-1 running Strata.
Exactly what you had: write your backup back in backup mode (Recovery, below), with the tool that made it
(MvaveFM1Unbricker, jl-uboot-tool, the FM-1 Transporter or flipper-fm1-recovery). Write only from 0x4000 up, never
the boot area.

Recovery
If no updater can reach the FM-1, put it in backup mode, where the chip itself accepts a backup or firmware over
USB:

OCT− and OCT+ held for 5 seconds on Strata or Felucca, or the SysEx message
F0 22 24 35 7D F7 on the FM-1's USB MIDI port (as on the official firmware). With Strata V0.87 the computer may
show an unknown USB device instead of the disk.
The FM-1 Transporter or a Flipper Zero with flipper-fm1-recovery, which work at power-on whatever the
firmware does. Use one of them if the FM-1 doesn't appear as a disk on the computer.

Switching the FM-1 off and on leaves backup mode. In backup mode, the restore tools (MvaveFM1Unbricker, the FM-1
Transporter, flipper-fm1-recovery) write only the firmware area and check it; none of them writes the boot area.

A write stopped (cable out, browser closed): don't switch the FM-1 off. Reconnect and press Find the FM-1
again; the page finishes the write.
STRATA CRASH on the screen: Strata restarts after 4 s. A second crash within 30 s of starting puts the FM-1 in
backup mode by itself.
A frozen screen: the watchdog restarts it within about 8 s; two such starts put it in backup mode.

Troubleshooting
No sound, or the wrong sound



Check

SCL + OCT−, ARP + OCT−

a drum track's HOME, DUCK knob


MIDI arrives on Strata's channel
SETTINGS > MIDI > CHANNEL


A sound stops the FM-1 at power-on
Hold HOME while switching on



Controls

A knob does nothing: a playing clip may have recorded moves of that parameter, which take over while it plays.
Stop the clip, or clear the motion on CLIP > TOOLS.
PRESETS doesn't open the presets: on looper pages it chooses the track, on a drum track the drum.
A button only closed a window: with a window open, the first press of another button closes it.
A reset didn't happen: hold the button and OCT− for the full 5 seconds.
The screen or LEDs are dark: SETTINGS > POWER > SCREEN OFF AFTER (any control wakes it), SCREEN > LIGHTS.
Crackles: too much unison and too many effects at once; Strata trims them by itself. Use fewer unison copies or
effects.
Everything feels wrong: SETTINGS > WIPE resets the settings; presets and projects stay.

The processor. Eight voices with two oscillators and a filter fit comfortably. Big unison with every effect does
not, so a guard steps in by itself: first the oldest notes lose unison copies, then the costliest effects get lighter,
then a voice is released, each with a fade. Fewer unison copies, fewer effects (REVERB costs most) or fewer VOICES

Not yet: a separate sound for each synth track (all synth tracks play the one sound loaded), sending knob CCs or
clock over MIDI, and putting the drums through the effects. MIDI out on the jack isn't possible: the FM-1's jack is an
input only.

changes.html.title: Changes
changes.html.body:
Changes
What each version changed, newest first.
Book rewritten: condensed, one-page guide
The book now matches Strata V0.87 at commit 3f869d7. The Guide is one page of feature cards, the cheat sheet is laid out
wide, and the Manual is shorter, with steps first. SCL's unused MIDI page is gone from the firmware.
V0.87
Drums. Any drum row can use any of seven models (ANALOG, PUNCH, FM, CHIP, NOISE, METAL, WAVE), on DRUM's new MODEL
page. 64 factory drum presets in eight categories (EDIT twice on DRUM), six factory kits (808, 909, LO-FI,
VIDEO GAME, TRAP, DRUM & BASS: EDIT twice on KIT or HOME), and your own library of 64 drum presets and 16
kits. EUCLID fills a row with a Euclidean rhythm.
Interface.

SAVE opens the SAVE window (SAVE, SAVE AS NEW, CANCEL).
ENV or LFO twice opens the assign window, with a POLARITY for each matrix slot.
Resets are a menu button + OCT− held 5 s.
HOME twice opens SETTINGS, which gained WIPE and LIGHTS; HOME held 5 s opens DEBUG.
EDIT twice opens the wavetable list. The MATRIX moved to EDIT.
Looper: tracks as rows on CLIPS, SONG on LOOP, the projects as a list (SEQ twice), new and deleted clips
with SEQ + OCT+ / OCT−, TAKE (REC twice), tap tempo (GLO
held + PLAY).

Earlier versions



Version
What it added




V0.86
The drum editor (DRUM, KIT); one screen layout; HOME's mixer pages; the presets list; looper SPEED and TOOLS; double presses; the help map


V0.85
Drum tracks: eight drums, accents, chance and ratchet, the step grid, the DUCK sidechain


V0.8
The 8-track looper: scenes, takes, overdubs, recorded knob moves, launch pad, mixer, SONG, projects


V0.75
The arpeggiator with sixteen steps; one button grammar for every menu; strum


V0.7
Chords: KEY and FREE modes, voicing, BASS


V0.67
Larger, clearer screens; VALUES pages; four more themes


V0.66
The STRATA screen design; smoother effect changes; faster screen and keys


V0.6
The effects chain and seven new effects


V0.5
The first Strata to run on an FM-1: the wavetable engine, presets, MIDI, USB audio
